note: Which vanilla component checks a React spec now carries. Curated, and checked by scripts/audit_check_port.py: the counts are re-read from the suites on every run, and every named test must exist in the named spec. The vanilla suites stay the regression net until R6. Revised 17 September 2026: the vanilla suites were removed in R6, so the counts below are the ledger's record and scripts/audit_port_ledger.py holds the names to account on every run. The last nine checks are ported too.

tests: renders a retrieved answer with its value, its source and its window
marks a conversational reply as having read no source and shows no fact table
lets the browser read the direction of the answer sentence
names what a continuation carried and what it changed
sets a held answer apart from a retrieved one
states the language downgrade in words rather than passing as answered
draws an uncovered part of the window as a gap and says so
shows the first reading and the stages while a turn works, and stops on request
returns the question to the box and states the server message when a turn fails
unfolds more of the evidence in the full register, and remembers the choice
falls back to the conversational register when the stored value is unreadable
offers only the languages whose writing this project measured, sorted by name
does not treat a written language as speakable unless speech was verified
names the source, the retrieval time and the method in one chain
offers every candidate the engine sent for a clarification
reads the resolved point out of the packet, and reports it absent when there is none
deletes a stored conversation through the local route only, and says when the delete failed
offers Collect fresh evidence for an answer with a resolved point, and asks for that exact point
offers no collection control for an answer with no resolved point
has no component reaching for fetch outside the api client
sends the session token on every request the client makes
sends one question with only the request keys the engine accepts
keeps the conversation id on a follow-up and never sends the rejected entity_id key
carries the workspace token on every request the surface makes
asks the server to cancel the turn in flight and reports its own reply
reports a full queue as a bounded queue rather than a generic failure
asks for a reload when the workspace token is no longer held
names the local evidence store when that store is unavailable
returns a refused question to the box and sends it again when the reader asks
starts a new conversation without sending a question and forgets the identifier
lists the stored conversations and filters them by their first question
refuses an empty question without sending anything
names the state a failed read left the reader in, not only the server sentence

suites.note: Complete: every one of the fourteen checks has a React counterpart. The turn spec holds the accepted request keys, the conversation id a follow-up keeps, the bounded queue, cancellation and its reply, the new conversation and the ledger with its search; the card spec holds the selection id a chosen place returns and the resolved point read from the packet; the parity spec holds the local delete; the field builder checks hold the editable box the builder never submits; and the page spec holds the refused empty question and the split between an expired token and an unavailable store, each stated as its own state with the action it calls for. None of the checks was retired.

The card specs hold the answer-first headline, the ruler and its segments and readout, the receipt, the bounded volume, the clarification with its selection id, the language downgrade, the held warning, the raw-packet inspector, the stage readout, the edition labelling, the two-product comparison, the quick replies, the provisional first reading, the continuation carrying, the register and the conversational labelling; the gap spec holds the computed value (and that a source comparison is a difference), the airport report and its type, the series receipt, task accounting and the warning day; and the page spec holds the class-name leak rule. suites.note: Complete: every one of the thirty-three checks has a React counterpart. The surface specs hold the renderer registry, the forecast chart, the Alt+hint contract, the plans panel, the watch inbox, the theme cycle, the palette with its place search and stored conversations, the routed names including the hyphenated route, the fresh and unknown route, compare side by side without ranking, empty compare, the token on every request, the map pointer readout, the city working place and the district keyboard cursor, the view transition, pinned places and the loading shapes; and the warning specs hold the district-day detail with its published hazard wording, the CAP relay assessment in its own block with the rule that reference resolution never authorises dissemination, the alert brief left to the product when no day is named, and the per-product collection-health rows behind the topbar chip.
